# Frontend Architecture — react-redux-realworld-example-app
**Date:** 2026-07-26  
**Standard applied:** GLD-STD-008@1 (Airbnb JavaScript Style Guide)

---

## 1. Framework & Entry Points

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Framework** | React 16.3.0 (class components only; no hooks) |
| **State** | Redux 3.6.0 via `react-redux` 5.0.7 |
| **Routing** | React Router 4 / `react-router-redux` (alpha) |
| **HTTP** | `superagent` wrapped in `superagent-promise` (`src/agent.js`) |
| **Build** | `react-scripts` 1.1.1 (Create React App, **ejected-capable but not ejected**) |
| **Entry point** | `src/index.js:11` — `ReactDOM.render` mounts `<Provider store>` → `<ConnectedRouter>` → `<App>` |

### Routes (declared in `src/components/App.js:58–68`)

| Path | Component |
|---|---|
| `/` | `Home` |
| `/login` | `Login` |
| `/register` | `Register` |
| `/editor` / `/editor/:slug` | `Editor` |
| `/article/:id` | `Article` |
| `/settings` | `Settings` |
| `/@:username` | `Profile` |
| `/@:username/favorites` | `ProfileFavorites` |

---

## 2. Component & State Map

### Component Tree

```
index.js
└── Provider (Redux store)
    └── ConnectedRouter
        └── App  [connected]                          App.js
            ├── Header                                Header.js
            │   ├── LoggedOutView  (inline function)
            │   └── LoggedInView   (inline function)
            ├── Home  [connected]                     Home/index.js
            │   ├── Banner                            Home/Banner.js
            │   ├── MainView  [connected]             Home/MainView.js
            │   │   ├── YourFeedTab   (inline fn)
            │   │   ├── GlobalFeedTab (inline fn)
            │   │   ├── TagFilterTab  (inline fn)
            │   │   └── ArticleList                   ArticleList.js
            │   │       ├── ArticlePreview [connected] ArticlePreview.js
            │   │       └── ListPagination [connected] ListPagination.js
            │   └── Tags                              Home/Tags.js
            ├── Article  [connected]                  Article/index.js
            │   ├── ArticleMeta                       Article/ArticleMeta.js
            │   │   └── ArticleActions [connected]    Article/ArticleActions.js
            │   └── CommentContainer                  Article/CommentContainer.js
            │       ├── CommentInput [connected]      Article/CommentInput.js
            │       └── CommentList                   Article/CommentList.js
            │           └── Comment                   Article/Comment.js
            │               └── DeleteButton [connected] Article/DeleteButton.js
            ├── Editor  [connected]                   Editor.js
            │   └── ListErrors                        ListErrors.js
            ├── Login   [connected]                   Login.js
            │   └── ListErrors
            ├── Register [connected]                  Register.js
            │   └── ListErrors
            ├── Settings [connected]                  Settings.js
            │   ├── SettingsForm (local class)
            │   └── ListErrors
            ├── Profile [connected]                   Profile.js
            │   ├── EditProfileSettings (inline fn)
            │   ├── FollowUserButton    (inline fn)
            │   └── ArticleList
            └── ProfileFavorites [connected]          ProfileFavorites.js
                └── (inherits Profile render)
```

**Maximum depth observed:** 10 levels  
(`App → Article → CommentContainer → CommentList → Comment → DeleteButton`)

### Redux Store Slices (`src/reducer.js`)

| Slice | Reducer file | Primary consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `common` | `reducers/common.js` | `App`, `Home`, `MainView`, `Profile` |
| `auth` | `reducers/auth.js` | `Login`, `Register` |
| `article` | `reducers/article.js` | `Article` |
| `articleList` | `reducers/articleList.js` | `MainView`, `Profile` |
| `editor` | `reducers/editor.js` | `Editor` |
| `home` | `reducers/home.js` | `Home`, `MainView` |
| `profile` | `reducers/profile.js` | `Profile`, `ProfileFavorites` |
| `settings` | `reducers/settings.js` | `Settings` |
| `router` | `react-router-redux` | `App` (push navigation) |

### Middleware chain (`src/store.js:17–20`)

`routerMiddleware` → `promiseMiddleware` → `localStorageMiddleware` [→ `redux-logger` in dev]

`promiseMiddleware` (`src/middleware.js:10–47`) intercepts any action whose `payload` is a Promise, resolves it, then re-dispatches the action — this is the sole async mechanism.

---

## 3. Structural Risks

### SR-1 · Deprecated lifecycle methods — all page-level components (High)
**Observed:** `componentWillMount` is used in **7 files** and `componentWillReceiveProps` in **3 files**:

| File | Methods |
|---|---|
| `src/components/App.js:34,42` | `componentWillReceiveProps`, `componentWillMount` |
| `src/components/Editor.js:73,83` | `componentWillReceiveProps`, `componentWillMount` |
| `src/components/Settings.js:41,52` | `componentWillMount`, `componentWillReceiveProps` |
| `src/components/Home/index.js:31` | `componentWillMount` |
| `src/components/Article/index.js:22` | `componentWillMount` |
| `src/components/Profile.js:78` | `componentWillMount` |
| `src/components/ProfileFavorites.js:19` | `componentWillMount` |

Both methods were marked `UNSAFE_` in React 16.3 (the installed version) and removed in React 18. Since all API calls are initiated here, migrating to React 18 will silently drop all data-fetching. Migration target: `componentDidMount` / `componentDidUpdate`.

### SR-2 · Direct store import inside a connected component (Medium)
**Observed:** `src/components/App.js:15,37` imports `store` directly from `../store` and calls `store.dispatch(push(nextProps.redirectTo))` bypassing Redux's `connect` / `mapDispatchToProps`. This creates a hidden coupling to the singleton store, makes the component untestable in isolation, and defeats the contract that `connect` provides.

### SR-3 · Class inheritance as a code-sharing mechanism (Medium)
**Observed:** `src/components/ProfileFavorites.js:18` — `class ProfileFavorites extends Profile`. React's own documentation discourages component inheritance; composition is the intended pattern. The inherited `render()` from `Profile` is not visible in `ProfileFavorites`, making the rendered output opaque to a reader of that file. `Profile` also has a dual named+default export (`Profile.js:170`) specifically to enable this pattern.

### SR-4 · `Object.assign` instead of spread — multiple files (Low, GLD-STD-008@1 §3.8)
**Observed** — GLD-STD-008@1 rule 3.8 requires object spread `{...obj}` over `Object.assign`:

| File:Line | Issue |
|---|---|
| `src/agent.js:45` | `Object.assign({}, article, { slug: undefined })` |
| `src/components/Editor.js:66` | `Object.assign(article, slug)` — **also mutates the first argument** |
| `src/components/Settings.js:25` | `Object.assign({}, state, { [field]: ev.target.value })` |
| `src/components/Settings.js:32` | `Object.assign({}, this.state)` |
| `src/components/Settings.js:43` | `Object.assign(this.state, {…})` — **directly mutates `this.state`**, a React anti-pattern |
| `src/components/Settings.js:54` | `Object.assign({}, this.state, {…})` |

The `Editor.js:66` and `Settings.js:43` cases are also correctness bugs, not just style violations.

### SR-5 · Reducers using `const` inside `switch` without block scope (Low)
**Observed:** `src/reducers/common.js:40` and `src/reducers/article.js:27` declare `const` directly inside a `case` arm without a block `{}`. In strict mode this can produce lexical-scoping surprises across fall-through arms. Standard remedy: wrap each `case` body in `{ }`.

### SR-6 · No code splitting / lazy loading (Unverified — no bundle profiler run)
**Observed:** All 8 route-level components (`Home`, `Article`, `Editor`, `Login`, `Register`, `Settings`, `Profile`, `ProfileFavorites`) are eagerly imported at the top of `App.js:7–13`. There is no `React.lazy` or `React.Suspense` usage anywhere in the codebase. **Inferred** risk: the entire application JS is delivered in a single chunk on first load.

### SR-7 · `console.log` left in production middleware (Low, GLD-STD-008@1; OWASP note)
**Observed:** `src/middleware.js:23` — `console.log('RESULT', res)` and `src/middleware.js:33` — `console.log('ERROR', error)` run unconditionally in every environment including production. The `res` object is the raw API response body, which may include user tokens or profile data. These should be gated behind a `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` guard or removed.  
_(GLD-STD-009@1 — OWASP Logging — applies; the values logged are not confirmed to be free of sensitive data. Full review against that standard is recommended before making a determination.)_

## 4. Accessibility Findings

**No `aria-*` attributes and no `role` attributes exist anywhere in the codebase** (confirmed by exhaustive search). The following concrete issues were observed in markup:

### A11Y-1 · All form inputs lack associated `<label>` elements (High)
**Observed:** Every `<input>` and `<textarea>` across `Login.js`, `Register.js`, `Editor.js`, `Settings.js`, and `CommentInput.js` relies solely on a `placeholder` attribute. Placeholders disappear on focus and are not read as labels by screen readers.

| File | Elements |
|---|---|
| `src/components/Login.js:63,72` | Email input, Password input |
| `src/components/Register.js:70,79,88` | Username, Email, Password inputs |
| `src/components/Editor.js:107,116,125,135` | Title, Description, Body textarea, Tags input |
| `src/components/Settings.js:70,79,88,98,108` | Image URL, Username, Bio, Email, Password |
| `src/components/Article/CommentInput.js:35` | Comment textarea |

WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) are implicated.

### A11Y-2 · Clickable `<i>` icons without keyboard access or accessible name (High)
**Observed:**

| File:Line | Element | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `src/components/Article/DeleteButton.js:20` | `<i className="ion-trash-a" onClick={del}>` | Clickable icon; no `role="button"`, no `tabIndex`, no accessible name |
| `src/components/Editor.js:149` | `<i className="ion-close-round" onClick={this.removeTagHandler(tag)}>` | Same — tag removal is inaccessible by keyboard |

Keyboard-only and screen reader users cannot trigger these actions.

### A11Y-3 · `<a href="">` used as interactive button (Medium)
**Observed** in 5 places — navigation tabs and tag links use `<a href="">` with `onClick` and `ev.preventDefault()`:

| File:Line | Usage |
|---|---|
| `src/components/Home/MainView.js:16` | "Your Feed" tab |
| `src/components/Home/MainView.js:35` | "Global Feed" tab |
| `src/components/Home/MainView.js:51` | Tag filter tab |
| `src/components/Home/Tags.js:18` | Each tag pill |
| `src/components/ListPagination.js:46` | Page number link |

An empty `href=""` navigates to the page root if JS fails. These should use `<button>` (tabs, tag pills) or real `href` values (pagination). The pagination `<li>` also has an `onClick` handler (`ListPagination.js:43`) while the child `<a>` has the `href` — click target and semantic element are misaligned.

### A11Y-4 · `<nav>` in `ListPagination` lacks an accessible name (Medium)
**Observed:** `src/components/ListPagination.js:30` — `<nav>` element has no `aria-label`. When a page has multiple `<nav>` landmarks (e.g., main nav + pagination), screen readers cannot distinguish them without labels.

### A11Y-5 · `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` article body — XSS and AT risk (Medium)
**Observed:** `src/components/Article/index.js:38,60` — the article body is rendered as raw HTML via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. The `marked` call uses `{ sanitize: true }`, but the `sanitize` option was **deprecated and removed** in `marked` 1.x (the installed version is `^0.3.6`, so it may still work, but the deprecation warning itself signals fragility). Injected HTML could contain non-semantic or ARIA-breaking markup.

---

## 5. Performance Smells

All items in this section are **Unverified** — no profiler or bundle analyser was run.

### P-1 · No route-level code splitting (Unverified)
**Mechanism:** All 8 page components are statically imported in `App.js:7–13`. The entire application — including the article editor, settings page, etc. — is downloaded on every first visit regardless of which route is accessed. React 16+ supports `React.lazy` + `React.Suspense` for splitting by route. No splitting is present.

### P-2 · Inline function creation on every render in list components (Unverified)
**Mechanism:** In several list-rendering `map` callbacks, closures are created per-item per-render:

| File:Line | Pattern |
|---|---|
| `src/components/Home/Tags.js:11` | `const handleClick = ev => {…}` created inside `tags.map(tag => …)` |
| `src/components/ListPagination.js:36` | `const onClick = ev => {…}` created inside `range.map(v => …)` |
| `src/components/Editor.js:51` | `this.removeTagHandler = tag => () => …` — outer handler correct, but returns a new fn per render |

These do not invalidate `React.PureComponent` optimisations on child components (none are used here), but they do create throwaway allocations each render cycle.

### P-3 · Missing `key` stability for tag lists (Unverified)
**Mechanism:** Tag lists in `Article/index.js:68` and `ArticlePreview.js:67` use the tag string as `key`. If a user edits tags in the editor, or if duplicate tags are possible, React may incorrectly reuse DOM nodes.

### P-4 · `promiseMiddleware` mutates the action object (Unverified — correctness risk)
**Mechanism:** `src/middleware.js:24` — `action.payload = res` reassigns a property on the dispatched action object. This works with Redux's current synchronous dispatch, but mutation of in-flight objects can cause subtle bugs if any middleware caches or logs the action before resolution.

### P-5 · No memoisation of `mapStateToProps` selectors (Unverified)
**Mechanism:** Several `mapStateToProps` functions spread entire state slices (e.g. `...state.home`, `...state.articleList`, `...state.editor`, `...state.auth`). Without `reselect`-style memoisation, any change to those slices triggers a re-render of all connected consumers, even if the specific props they use haven't changed.
